name: ESP32-2432S024N (Cheap Yellow Display, 2.4in, N variant)
summary: The tightest board ESP-OS runs on, and the one that sets tier 0. Also sold as HW-950.

render.reason: About 20KB of free heap at steady state with WiFi and BLE up. A 320x240 RGB565 framebuffer is 150KB and LVGL's own working set is tens of KB on top of that, so neither fits. A 320x240 8-bit indexed buffer is 76.8KB, allocated once at boot before WiFi fragments the heap, and flushed a line at a time through a 640-byte RGB565 staging buffer. This is the same arrangement the cyd24 terminal and the six-game arcade already run.

display.pixel_format_reason: RGB565 straight down the wire, two bytes per pixel.
display.clock_reason: 40MHz is the rate the proven cyd24 firmware runs. MISO is bound on this board (GPIO12) because the module wires it, and a bound MISO caps what the ESP32 SPI driver will actually clock, so 80MHz would not be honoured even if the panel tolerated it. Do not raise this without re-testing the whole panel, not just a test card.

bluetooth_keyboard.reason: NimBLE is 19KB of heap; Bluedroid is 83KB, which is instant OOM on a board with 20KB free. Release classic-BT memory and bring BLE up BEFORE WiFi, then WiFi.setSleep(true). The K809 keyboard bonds to whichever board it paired with last.

touch.absent_reason: This is the N variant: no touch controller is fitted at all, despite the module looking exactly like a touchscreen. Two boards were probed for 60 seconds each with an I2C sweep and an XPT2046 transfer on every candidate pin set, including the classic CLK25 MOSI32 MISO39 CS33 wiring. Nothing answered on either. Do not probe again.

panel_id_register.note: Not attempted. The ILI9488 boards proved that a controller ID read is not something to build on, so nothing in ESP-OS reads one.

distinguishing_notes: 2.4 inch panel in a yellow PCB with a microSD slot on the left edge.
Silkscreened ESP32-2432S024N, sometimes HW-950. The trailing N is the variant letter and the only thing separating it from the R variant, which does have an XPT2046 touch chip.
CH340 bridge, so it enumerates as /dev/cu.usbserial-* rather than a native USB device.
identification.confirm_prompt: Is this the 2.4in Cheap Yellow Display, and does the silkscreen end in N rather than R? The R variant has touch and this profile does not configure it.

gotchas.text: There is no touch controller. Every input path has to come from the BLE keyboard, the BOOT button, USB serial or the board's own web page.
Bluedroid does not fit. 83KB against 19KB for NimBLE, on a board with about 20KB free at steady state. Linking Bluedroid gives an out-of-memory crash during BLE init, not a subtle degradation.
Release classic-BT memory and initialise BLE before WiFi. The other order leaves the heap too fragmented for the BLE allocation to land.
The RGB LED is active low. Pins left as inputs or driven high are off; the naive all-pins-high-is-white assumption gives you a permanently white LED.
About 20KB free heap at steady state with WiFi and BLE up. Any new subsystem has to be measured against that, not estimated.
Panel is on HSPI and the microSD is on VSPI (SCK18 MISO19 MOSI23 CS5). They do not share a bus, so no bus lock is needed between them.
